sender.en: “Someone you met on a dating site or social media”

name.en: Romance scam: an online partner who needs money

how.en: Criminals create fake profiles on dating sites and social media, sometimes with AI-made photos. They build trust over weeks, develop strong feelings quickly and want to move the chat to another app. They always have a reason they can’t video call or meet. Then they ask for money for an emergency, travel or medical care.

text.en: You meet someone online who seems perfect and falls for you quickly.
They want to move the chat off the dating app and avoid video calls.
They build trust over weeks with details about their life and work.
They ask for money for an emergency, travel or medical bills.
I've never felt like this about anyone, my love. I want to come to see you but my bank account is frozen here. Could you help me with the flight? I will pay you back as soon as I land.

en: met someone online asking for money
boyfriend online needs money for flight
dating site match won't video call
online partner asked for bank transfer
never met him but sent money
Strong feelings very quickly, from someone you have never met.
Always a reason they can’t video call or meet.
Any request for money or bank details.
Never send money or bank details to someone you have only met online.
Stay in the dating app’s messages and talk to someone you trust.
If you sent money, call your bank straight away and report it to Report Fraud.

sources.title: Campaign to protect viewers from romance fraud launched by National Crime Agency and Freeview channel Great Romance
